svg.title: The gyro: heading from turning rate
svg.desc: Animated. A robot seen from above, with the gyro at its center, turns one full turn counter-clockwise from where it was zeroed, and a blue arc around it grows to show its heading. On the right, the turning rate the gyro measures rises, holds and falls; thin slices under it fill in as a cursor sweeps across, and the heading graph below, the sum of every little turn so far, climbs to one full turn. Small errors add up: a gyro that reads 1% short is 3.6 degrees off after one full turn, and 36 degrees after ten. Field-relative driving, odometry and every auto depend on that heading.
svg.text: The gyro: heading from turning rate
It measures how fast the robot turns and adds it up into a heading.
Turning rate: what the gyro measures
Small errors add up: a gyro that reads 1% short is 3.6 degrees off
after one full turn, and 36 degrees after ten.
Field-relative driving, odometry and every auto depend on that heading.
